next_step: Run 2-week latency POC with streaming + tool-calls; finalize Dedicated sizing if SLOs met
notes: Summary: Mid-market product company building an embedded chat assistant + orchestration layer for task automation inside their product. Primary focus = sub-200ms token latency for streaming UX; tool-calling must be <= 300ms median extra overhead.

Background: Started with prototype using competitor hosted API; hit cost and unpredictable latency under burst. Looking at Redwood Hosted API first for predictability and streaming primitives, then evaluating Dedicated for steady-state cost + data isolation.
POC activity: Completed hosted API sandbox test (7-day). Observed streaming stability but saw tail latency spikes ~600ms on long tool call flows during synthetic load spike (see ff_2026-02-18_8342).

Evaluation goals: 1) Verify streaming SLOs (p50 < 120ms, p95 < 280ms) under 30 TPS; 2) Validate tool-calling orchestration hooks (structured tool outputs + retry semantics); 3) Ensure prompt/eval regression gating works with A/B + canary rollouts.

Quality gating: Wants prompt-level evals tied to canary deploys — automatic rollback on >3% quality regression vs control set. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization + batching tradeoffs.
Security: Requires SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to Splunk, KMS integration for encryption-at-rest; legal has an open question about data residency for EU customers (could push Dedicated/VPC).
Quotes: 'We need predictable streaming UX — users drop off if responses stutter' (Product lead). 'Cost matters but not at expense of latency.'

Meetings: 2026-02-18 - Hosted API demo + stress test (Samir, Maya, Eng lead). 2026-02-25 - Deep dive on tool-calling & structured outputs (SE session). 2026-03-01 - Legal & Security sync re: KMS + data residency.

POC findings: 1) Batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize reduced tokens/sec cost by ~18% in test. 2) KV cache warmed flows meet p50 targets; cold-start for long contexts needs Dedicated kernel tuning. 3) Canary A/B hook works but needs easier owner-defined eval thresholds and alerting.
Commercial: Interested in a Dedicated sizing quote (3 x A40-equivalent capacity) and 12-month commit discount. Wants pricing scenarios showing break-even vs Hosted at 750M tokens/month.
Open action items: SE to run 48-hour burst test with simulated tool-calls and raw latency traces; Product to share canonical eval prompt set; Legal to confirm KMS key ownership model.
Next step owner: SE (Maya) to schedule burst POC by 2026-03-15. AE (Samir) to send Dedicated preliminary pricing matrix by 2026-03-12.
Risk/Blockers notes: If Dedicated pricing isn't within 15% of forecasted cost, they will extend Hosted POC and re-assess. Data residency questions could push timeline to Q3 procurement.
